bib.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models

read.skipped: none; the PDF has 14 pages and no appendix (references skimmed)

question: Can a transformer learn to dynamically allocate a fixed, smaller compute budget across tokens and layers without losing language-modeling quality?
hypothesis: Certain tokens need less processing than others, and a learned router can identify them so that capacity can be cut without hurting performance.
contributions: Top-k expert-choice routing between a block (self-attention + MLP) and a residual path, giving a static graph with known tensor sizes
isoFLOP analysis showing MoD variants that beat or match the optimal baseline with fewer FLOPs per forward pass
Two ways to sample autoregressively despite non-causal top-k: auxiliary BCE loss or auxiliary MLP predictor
Integration with MoE (MoDE), staged and integrated

method.summary: Each routed block has a linear router that emits a scalar per token; the top-k tokens per sequence go through self-attention and MLP, the rest pass via the residual. Block output is scaled by the router weight so the router gets gradients. Trained from scratch at several isoFLOP budgets and compared to isoFLOP-optimal vanilla transformers.

limits: Dataset, tokenizer, optimizer, learning rate, layers/hidden sizes and training tokens are not stated, so the run cannot be reproduced.
Speed-ups are expressed as FLOPs per forward pass and training step speed; no wall-clock measurement of autoregressive sampling latency is reported despite the abstract's sampling claim.
Predictor accuracy is quoted as 99% in text and 97% in Fig 6 caption; no per-layer breakdown.
Memory/KV-cache savings are anticipated but 'not studied extensively'.
Only decoder-only models up to 3B parameters, no downstream task evaluation, no seeds or error bars.
Preliminary entropy correlation of routing is only suggestive.
